questionText: How do you choose between REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and WebSocket for your API?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can choose an API technology from interaction direction, duration, client ownership, contract needs, caching, and operations instead of claiming one universal winner.
outOfScope: A claim that one technology must serve every boundary

claims.statement: REST supplies a resource-and-representation interaction model whose HTTP use can expose standard method, status, validator, cache, and content-negotiation semantics.
GraphQL operations select fields from a typed schema, and a supported subscription operation produces a response stream without the core specification requiring one transport.
Current gRPC core documentation defines unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional-streaming service methods from a shared service definition.
claims.notes: The living documentation was reviewed on 2026-09-09.

claims.statement: RFC 6455 defines WebSocket as a protocol enabling two-way communication after an opening handshake, with application messages carried over the resulting connection.

Selecting among these technologies is an architecture decision based on message shape, direction, duration, clients, infrastructure, and operations; their definitions do not establish one universal speed or suitability ranking.

examples.title: One product using distinct technologies at earned boundaries

validation.command: Trace each example boundary to its dominant interaction and verify that the text labels the architecture as illustrative
validation.expected: Each mapping is plausible without being presented as a required architecture or speed ranking

visuals.title: Dominant interaction, candidate technology, and operating check

notes: SSE, webhooks, and polling are presented as simpler alternatives in suitable directions and frequencies, not as equivalent protocols.

review.notes: Definitions were checked against Fielding/RFC 9110, GraphQL October 2021, current gRPC core documentation, and RFC 6455; the final selection matrix is explicitly architecture guidance.
